critical_code_review_comments: server.py websocket capacity guard has an await boundary between pre-check and final player insertion; this can violate hard total-cap guarantees under concurrency.
Capacity logic mixes human-precheck and post-accept bot eviction; guard should be centralized with a single lock/transactional section.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin settings were restored to baseline after UI run (all bosses active, day, normal, bot_count 0). Auth cookies and origin/csrf/rate-limit regression remain green in serial suite. Focus next on fixing/verifying websocket total-cap race under concurrent joins.
rca of the issue: RCA (total-cap race): In websocket(), human-cap is checked before await ws.accept and prior to add_player. Concurrent joins can both pass precheck at 199 humans; first may evict a bot and add human, second may then add another human without available bot to evict, temporarily allowing >200 total. Mitigation: guard admission in a shared async lock and re-check+evict+insert atomically, or reserve slot at /join and commit/rollback at ws connect.
